entry.title: C++26: std::constant_wrapper
entry.summary: There’s a fundamental gap in C++ that trips up everyone who reaches for it: you can’t pass a constexpr value through a function boundary and have it remain constexpr on the other side. The value is known at compile time, the function is constexpr, but the parameter inside the function body is not a constant expression. entry.summary: In part 1 we looked at the new views C++26 adds, and in part 2 we covered the infrastructure improvements. This final part is about the biggest gap in C++20 ranges: you couldn’t run them in parallel. C++17 added execution policies to the classic std:: algorithms, but C++20 ranges never got them.
